extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors and peer reviewers of health / clinical research articles
extracted.subtask_description: Help authors/editors/peer reviewers identify which reporting guideline or checklist is appropriate for a manuscript based on its study type/design, and direct them to tools (EQUATOR database, GoodReports) and fillable checklists to submit with manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reporting guidelines / checklists
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting Guidelines and checklists have been developed for a wide variety of research types and study designs which set up the most important things readers need to know about your work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors frequently forget to report details important for readers; incomplete reporting can delay publication and stop work being used, cited or replicated. Use appropriate reporting guidelines to ensure essential details are reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomised trials — CONSORT (and extensions)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists CONSORT and its extensions as the primary reporting guideline for randomised trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observational studies — STROBE (and extensions)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STROBE and its extensions are the recommended reporting guideline(s) for observational study designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic reviews — PRISMA (and extensions)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRISMA (and related extensions) are recommended for reporting systematic reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study protocols — SPIRIT and PRISMA-P
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SPIRIT for trial protocols and PRISMA-P for systematic review protocols as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic / prognostic studies — STARD and TRIPOD
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For diagnostic accuracy and prognostic model studies, follow STARD or TRIPOD as indicated by study focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case reports — CARE (and extensions)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the CARE guideline (and any applicable extensions) when preparing clinical case reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical practice guidelines — AGREE and RIGHT
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AGREE and RIGHT are cited as reporting/quality frameworks for clinical practice guideline development and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative research — SRQR and COREQ
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRQR and COREQ are recommended for reporting qualitative research studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal pre-clinical studies — ARRIVE
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the ARRIVE guidelines for reporting animal research to improve transparency and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality improvement studies — SQUIRE (and extensions)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SQUIRE (and any extensions) when reporting quality improvement work in healthcare settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic evaluations — CHEERS (and extensions)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CHEERS and its extensions are recommended for reporting economic evaluation studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use tools/wizards to choose appropriate guideline (GoodReports)
rubrics_metrics.description: EQUATOR collaborated with Penelope Research to develop an online wizard (GoodReports) based on a flow chart to help authors, editors and peer reviewers find the most appropriate checklist and reporting guideline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GoodReports includes many commonly used reporting guidelines (16 in the first release) and directs users to online fillable checklists to submit alongside manuscripts. The tool supports using more than one guideline where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the EQUATOR Database to search guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: You can also search the EQUATOR Database of Reporting Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the wizard doesn't identify a guideline, use the searchable EQUATOR Database to find reporting guidelines relevant to your study type or specialty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult guidance on study types (CEBM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Read more about different study types on the website of Oxford’s Centre for Evidence-based Medicine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure about which guideline fits, consult authoritative descriptions of study types (e.g., CEBM) to match study design to the appropriate reporting guideline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be prepared to use more than one guideline
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilitating the use of more than one reporting guideline where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complex or hybrid studies may require more than one reporting guideline; the GoodReports project explicitly aims to facilitate using multiple applicable guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit completed/filled checklist with manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: GoodReports directs you to an online fillable version of the checklist to submit to a journal alongside your manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals may expect a completed checklist at submission; using the fillable checklist can streamline peer review and editorial checks.
